_banner: @spec       docs/DESIGN-V2.md#4 - next_boundary, the exact Move twin
@facts      Every nextBoundary below is ALSO asserted to be 06:00:00.000 or 18:00:00.000 UTC.
@forbidden  an operator-supplied close timestamp - close_ms is DERIVED

vectors.name: epoch-zero-skips-the-first-boundary
vectors.why: FINDING: since saturates to 0 below the offset, so the very first 06:00 is skipped and the answer is 18:00. Replicated from the Move source verbatim; unreachable after 1970-01-01 06:00 UTC.

vectors.name: exactly-06-00-returns-18-00
vectors.why: The boundary is STRICTLY next: standing exactly on 06:00 gives 18:00, never 06:00 again.

vectors.name: one-ms-before-06-00
vectors.why: Just before the morning boundary the answer is that same morning boundary.

vectors.name: one-ms-after-06-00
vectors.why: One ms past it, the answer has already moved to 18:00.

vectors.name: exactly-18-00-returns-next-06-00
vectors.why: The evening boundary rolls to the following morning.

vectors.name: midnight
vectors.why: Midnight resolves to the SAME morning, not the previous evening.

vectors.name: exactly-the-offset
vectors.why: 1970-01-01 06:00 UTC - the first reachable boundary, and the first input where since stops saturating.

vectors.name: one-ms-below-the-offset
vectors.why: The last input in the saturating region.

vectors.name: far-future
vectors.why: 2100-01-01 00:00 UTC - proves no drift accumulates over 130 years of periods.
